title: PR6066 signed halves admit exact restoration with a charged tape kernel
body:
## Result

One signed stochastic half from [PR #6066](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6066) now has an explicit reversible Boolean word and fixed-tape program. For every signed width W≥2, either sign and either resident coin, it returns the exact rounded value, preserves the coin, and retains the one parity bit needed to restore the dirty input. Reversing the program clears that residue and all W clean working cells. No extra arithmetic guard bit is required within the declared signed input range.

The literal tape program includes every head walk and both head returns. For instruction-word length L, each direction costs **2L+2 interpreter steps**, with 2W+2 binary data cells, W clean work bits, one retained parity, a read-only program of L+2 fixed-alphabet cells and a fixed finite interpreter. The program length is O(W²), and its preparation/storage are charged. For example, at W=64 the positive and negative directions cost 203,002 and 386,482 steps respectively. These are explicit baseline costs, not a faster tariff.

## Significance for researchers

This resolves the single signed-half lowering requested by [PR #6066](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6066), with separate integer, gate and tape semantics and a complete local scratch/guard/motion ledger. It provides a concrete primitive to price when composing the optimal retained-log boundary from [PR #6091](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6091). That composition, clean-work availability, resident random-bit delivery and the other scalar/native operations remain open; none is assigned zero cost.

## Validation

CPython 3.12 normal and optimized registered checks pass 2,032 exhaustive signed gate cases through eight bits, 324 literal tape forward/inverse round trips, and 96 larger-width guard cases through 128 bits. Checks include signed endpoints, exact residue/work/coin cleanup, every head return, gate counts, program hashes and rejection controls. Source binding confirms the historical prefix's 18 positive and 66 negative half sites. Exact committed-byte preflight passes at `39df190f3a8a04cccb88ef1a6ca9aad39ed0364d`; committed export integrity/input coverage also pass.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/reversible-signed-half-kernel
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/reversible-signed-half-kernel
```

Only an isolated research package is added. The resident coin and clean work are explicit caller preconditions. No full prefix/caller, physical sampler, native MOVE, selected cold replay, κ increase, independent human review or formal-kernel approval is claimed. The existing base navigation failures tracked by [PR #6050](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6050) remain separate.

## Open next questions

Install this kernel at one actual reached site with paid coin delivery, clean-work allocation, scalar layout and finite guard bounds. Then lower a rounded ADD and the other SCALEs, handle the inferred-residue sites of [PR #6091](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6091), and total the physical word's bill before claiming a supplier or exponent effect. A faster tape layout can be compared against this fully specified baseline.

Prepared by [zxv](https://github.com/zxv) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit [Nick Petalas](https://github.com/petalas)'s [PR #6026](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6026), [Ali Romman](https://github.com/aliromman)'s [PR #5599](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5599), [PR #6066](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6066)'s ABI and the retained source lineage. Ripple carries and reversible gate decompositions are classical; the signed stochastic-half/tape contract and source-relative invoice are the contribution. Apache-2.0.
